messages:
marta: heads-up: after pulling ruby-ffi 0.9.1 into the minimal sampleapp we use for onboarding, the process RAM steadily increases during batch embedding runs. anyone else hit this or have clues?

alex: not on my local machine yet. can you share how you ran it and a small repro?

marta: sure. run ./scripts/sample_embed_runner.sh with EMBED_COUNT=1500 and ruby 3.2.2. memory climbs ~8-12MB/min until OOM in my container. simplified loop i used:
```
1500.times do
  client.embeddings(input: "a" * 512)
end
```
object_space dump shows many FFI::Pointer-ish objects still live.

sam: this matches a change i landed in the native extension last month: we switched to storing a raw VALUE/char* to avoid a utf8 copy for perf. i think we forgot to rb_gc_register_address the VALUE, so GC isn't aware and pointers become roots but never freed.

jamie: that would definitely explain it. quick question: did you test with RUBY_GC_HEAP_GROWTH_FACTOR tweaks? could be GC frequency masking it.

marta: i tried both default GC and RUBY_GC_HEAP_GROWTH_FACTOR=1.3; didn't alter the leak trend. i made a minimal C snippet showing we keep a VALUE in a struct and never mark it.

leo: pinging from sampleapps maint — thanks for the repro. if the fix is only marking/registering the VALUE we can patch quickly. is there an existing PR?

marta: opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-ffi/pull/489 — change uses rb_gc_register_address for the stored VALUE and adds a stress spec (100k iterations) plus a 30s integration job in CI.

alex: pulling the branch now. quick local run looks way better; memory stabilizes. left two tiny style nits in the PR: prefer rb_gc_mark inside mark function vs register if we want to support per-object lifecycle.

sam: good point. register_address is simpler to audit but mark is better if objects are transient. which pattern do we prefer across our native ext codebase?

jamie: we standardized around a mark function for GC in other native extensions (see libnative/README). let's follow that for consistency and add a comment referencing the original perf change that removed the copy. also add a changelog entry so release notes are clear.

marta: updated PR to use rb_gc_mark in the mark hook and added commit referencing the perf commit hash. added changelog line: "fix: avoid native memory leak in embeddings via GC marking (ruby-ffi)"

leo: would be great to backport to the 0.8.x branch we ship in older onboarding images. can we release a 0.9.2 and backport patch to 0.8.9?

sam: yeah plan: cut a patch 0.9.2 for main, then cherry-pick a minimal fix to 0.8.x as 0.8.9. i'll handle the releases once PR is green.

jamie: LGTM, i'm leaving a short review and will assign sam for merge.

deploy-bot: deploy-queue: patch-release/0.9.2 queued to staging (artifact: ruby-ffi-0.9.2.gem). ETA ~10m.

alex: i'll run the staged gem against our minimal sampleapp matrix and the quickstart images.

sam: merged PR and published ruby-ffi 0.9.2 to internal gem server. cherry-pick applied to release/0.8.x as 0.8.9 and pushed a patch gem to the old images repo.

marta: verified the updated gems in our staging harness and the sampleapp; no memory growth under the same workload. thanks for the fast turnaround.

leo: great—i'll update the onboarding readme to mention the recommended gem versions and add a short note to the sampleapp troubleshooting section about monitoring memory during embed-heavy runs.

marta: thanks all! if anyone sees odd behavior on other ruby versions please tag me here. :tada:
